text: Due to the fact that the files that were submitted by the participants did not all follow the same naming pattern, the process of matching each file to the participant who had submitted it required additional work. This extra work was done manually, which means that the time recorded for the analysis included time spent on matching files as well as time spent on the analysis itself. For this reason, it would not be correct to interpret the recorded time as a measurement of analysis speed alone.
review: Clarify the naming problem, manual matching and consequence for interpreting analysis time.
Do not remove the distinction between total recorded time and analysis speed.
reference: Inconsistent participant filenames required manual matching. The recorded analysis time therefore included both file matching and analysis and cannot be interpreted as a measure of analysis speed alone.

text: Among the 18 households that took part, water use was about 12% lower during the trial than during the week before it. However, because of the fact that the weather was cooler during the trial and because there was no comparison group, it is not possible for us to say that the device was the reason for all of the reduction. The finding may justify a larger test, but it should not be taken as a guarantee of savings for other households.
review: Preserve the approximate reduction, baseline timing, weather confound, no control group and limited generalization.

text: The fact that an alarm did not go off should not be taken to mean that there was no fault, since the detector was not active during the first hour.
review: No alarm is not proof of no fault; preserve that the detector was inactive in the first hour.

text: The equation that was used in order to calculate the energy was $E=mc^2$, and the reason for choosing this equation is discussed in \cite{miller2022}. The discussion can be found by looking at \ref{sec:energy}.
review: Improve prose while retaining the exact equation, citation and reference.

text: The valve opens when pressure exceeds the configured threshold.
review: An unchanged answer is acceptable. Do not add a numeric threshold or reverse the condition.
